iconicAnchor.label: The Dial and modernist culture-journal traditions
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Editors, critics, writers, artists, and little-magazine publishers
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Dial archive establishes the culture review as an edited meeting of criticism, literature, visual art, reviews, and recurring issue identity rather than an undifferentiated long-form blog.

sources.title: The Dial
sources.publisher: Brigham Young University Modernist Short Story Project
supports: The journal archive documents an issue-based cultural publication carrying criticism, literature, and visual material.
Its contents support differentiated departments held together by masthead and editorial identity.

sources.title: Modernist Journals Project
supports: The project preserves periodical networks in which criticism, art, politics, reviews, and experimental writing circulated together.
The collection provides comparative evidence for issue rhythm and editorial identity beyond a single title.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches criticism, essay review mix, section identity, art text dialogue, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/culture-review/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
